title: Package install: POST /api/v1/packages installs a package with no protocol range unchecked and says so only in the server log (the install-local door now answers it)
body:
domain:server#5 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CYVV6fcAQrNTDQRvPb

Filed from PR #30409 (card #30326, server half), the dev's acceptance note "not covered" and the seat ACCEPT 6655279987. ⛔ Not a claim. Triage sets the grade.

**Business reason.** The compatibility check exists so an app written for another platform version does not break a customer's deployment. After PR #30409 the marketplace install door (`POST /api/v1/marketplace/install-local`) tells the installer when the check was skipped. The package install door `POST /api/v1/packages` still does not: the administrator who installs a package with no `engines.protocol` there reads only success, and only the server log says it was not checked.

**Reader who acts.** `domain:server`, `packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts` (~L1750, `assertProtocolCompat(manifest)`, its verdict dropped).

## What to do

Answer the same optional notice the install-local door answers (`protocolCheckSkipped`: `reason`, `packageId`, `protocolVersion`, `message`, plus `requiredRange` / `rangeSource` for `unparsed-range`), read from the verdict `assertProtocolCompat` now returns (`ProtocolCompatAdmitted`, PR #30409), never a second reading of the range. Omit it for a checked range. One spelling with the install-local door: share the mapping (`protocolCheckSkippedOf`) rather than restating it. Pin a no-range install, an unparsed range and a satisfied-range control.

Serial after PR #30409 merges. If the answer is a published `packages/spec` schema, report it rather than deciding in the PR (#30326's own rule). Dedupe: `packages install protocolCheckSkipped`, `POST /api/v1/packages engines.protocol`: none. **New.**
